answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with bonded identity. Each agent locks real collateral before it gets a vote, and that bond is slashed if it double-votes, so influence is bought rather than minted. Picture a market island: every vendor keeps a velvet purse of stake on the counter and signs a permanent basalt ledger of names. To forge a thousand voters an attacker must lock a thousand separate purses, and one detected cheat slashes them all. The cost therefore grows linearly with every fake identity, while an honest agent posts a single recoverable bond.
